title: SLO-driven handoff debug journal
content:
One-line summary:
SLO-triggered routing policy change (canary > 100ms p95) caused an aggressive handoff to regional fallbacks; cascade observed when egress limits + model-variant mismatches produced repeated fallbacks and token errors. Tracking commands we ran, snippets of logs, and hypotheses for root cause / mitigation.

Context and immediate impact:
- Time window: 2026-03-05 02:11:24 -> 02:39:10 UTC (28m)
- Affected customers: subset of hosted-api routes (chat.* and gen.*) in eu-west1 and us-west1 bursts
- Symptom: sudden p95 token-latency jump from ~90ms to ~420ms plus upstream 429/502s originating from fallback layer. No control-plane alerts initially.

Key request IDs (sample):
- req=20260305-02-13-7f8b: see logs below
- req=20260305-02-22-a10c

Commands tried (chronological):
1) curl tests against router with route hint header:
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Redwood-Route: region=eu-west1;policy=primary' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -D -
- Observed: 502 from proxy, response contains 'fallback-invoked: no-capacity-match' header.

2) kubectl on routing pool (us-west1-e):
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=route-adapter -o wide
kubectl -n redwood logs route-adapter-5f6c -c adapter --since=30m | egrep 'fallback|hand-off|circuit' -A3 -B1
- Snippet: 2026-03-05T02:15:12Z WARN route-adapter: handoff requestId=20260305-02-13-7f8b to fallback=regional-escort-us-east1 reason="p95>100ms, capacity=0"
- Followed by: ERROR kv-cache: fail to fetch prefix key, miss-rate=0.34

3) traceroute / tcpdump on egress path for a small repro pod:
traceroute -n 10.1.4.22
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 34.120.11.76 and port 443 -w /tmp/egress.pcap
- Observed intermittent retransmits and multiple TCP RSTs during 02:12-02:18 window.

4) rtrctl (internal) show routes and rate-limits:
rtrctl show policy active --route eu-west1
- Found: policy escort-decision had TTL 30s and aggressive egress_rate_limit=1200 tps configured for canary. Canary breached SLO -> route switch trigged for 11s windows repeatedly.

Service logs (selected snippets):
- [02:13:49] route-scheduler INFO: canary p95=137ms > SLO(100ms) -> mark unhealthy for 30s
- [02:13:50] smart-router INFO: handoff-start req=... to tier=regional-fallback; fallback-policy=escort
- [02:13:51] egress-proxy ERROR: max-connects reached for us-west1-egress (45/45) -> queueing
- [02:13:53] smart-router WARN: fallback-retry req=... attempt=2 -> variant-mismatch (model abc-v1 expected quantized but served as fp16)
- [02:14:02] billing-proxy ERROR: tokenize failure: MAX_TOKENS_EXCEEDED while upstream returned chunked 502

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Canary's short TTL + overly aggressive egress throttles caused oscillation: route flips created bursts to fallback regions that then hit egress/connect limits (cascade).
2) Model variant mismatch between primary and fallback (quantization/profile mismatch) resulted in repeated variant-conversion errors causing retries and added latency.
3) KV cache miss surge amplified latency; cache eviction policy tied to region-specific memory pressure (hot shards moved) produced miss-rate spike.
4) Underlying network flakiness (observed TCP RSTs) amplified the above, causing transient connection saturations and failed circuit-breaker recovery.

Reproduction steps (minimal repro):
1) Deploy a canary policy locally with TTL=30s and egress_rate_limit=1200, target eu-west1 primary.
2) Flood the canary with synthetic load at ~1500 rps (curl/batch) with medium tokens to push p95 over 100ms.
3) Observe handoff triggers; monitor egress-proxy connect counters + rtrctl show policy events.

Quick mitigations attempted (what we did):
- Increased egress-proxy connection pool temporarily in eu-west1 (from 45 -> 80) at 02:19 — slight improvement but still oscillating.
- Rolled back canary policy TTL to 3s (less stabilization window) at 02:24 -> temporarily reduced oscillation but reappeared when load spiked.
- Pin fallback model variant to same quantization profile as primary (patch PR #882) — reduced variant-mismatch errors but latency still high.

Remaining unknowns / checks to run:
- Confirm exact moment and cause of TCP RSTs: gcloud VPC flow logs and cloud provider peering metrics for 02:12-02:18.
- Investigate why KV cache miss-rate jumped from 0.04 -> 0.34: check cache-shard reallocation events, memory OOMs on cache nodes.
- Verify whether circuit-breaker thresholds triggered request-level retries at client side (SDK telemetry).

Follow-up action items (owners):
- Jin: collect egress-proxy connection histograms and share 1m-granularity metrics (due 2026-03-06)
- Ravi: run controlled repro with canary TTL=3s vs 30s and capture route switch timeline (due 2026-03-07)
- Maya (me): coordinate confluence write-up + link to PR882 and Linear REDW-3124 (due 2026-03-09)

Notes to self / debugging tips:
- When seeing repeated handoffs, check both route TTL and egress rate-limits — small TTLs + tight egress limits = oscillation hazard.
- Always verify model variant compatibility before allowing fallback to automatically serve; add a pre-deploy compatibility check in routing policy evaluator.
- If seeing high kv cache miss-rate coincident with handoffs, suspect cache-shard churn; look at redis/rocksdb memory events.

End of scratch journal. Will append additional logs and gcloud flow-logs when collected.
